info.name: InvoiceHub: download a claim-check file
info.description:
What a receiving system does with a claim-check webhook, step by step: find the event, read the link out of its body, download the file, and compare size and SHA-256 with what the webhook announced.

Run the requests in order (or run the collection). Needs the demo running on this machine.

**Why a copied link fails**
- The body is JSON, so the link contains `\"` (backslash and quote) when you copy it from a formatted view. The backslashes change a signed value: 403 AuthorizationFailure. Request 2 parses the JSON instead and turns the plain quotes into `%22`.
- The link lives 15 minutes (the `se=` part). Request 0 makes a fresh event.
- The link points at the Azurite emulator on this machine (127.0.0.1:<port>).

Requests 3 to 5 have *URL encoding* switched off on purpose: the URL is sent exactly as the platform signed it.

item.name: 0  Make a fresh claim-check event (then wait about 5 seconds)

request.description: A catalogue import: the report (about 600 bytes of JSON) is written to blob storage and the webhook carries a link to it. For the 50 MB file use POST /simulator/exports with { "tenant": "contoso", "sizeMegabytes": 50 }.

exec: console.log('Job ' + pm.response.json().jobId + ' is queued. Wait about 5 seconds, then run request 1.');

item.name: 1  Find the newest claim-check event in the receiver's inbox

request.description: The inbox lists what the receiver has been sent, newest first.

exec: pm.test('a claim-check event is there', () => pm.expect(hit, 'none yet: run request 0, wait a few seconds and send this again').to.exist);

item.name: 2  Read the link out of the event body

request.description: `body` is the webhook body exactly as received, a JSON document inside a JSON string. The script parses it, so no backslashes ever reach the link.

exec: // the link holds two plain double quotes (inside the signed rscd value); send them as %22, which is what any HTTP client does

pm.test('the link has not expired yet (15 minutes after the attempt)', () => pm.expect(new Date(data.download.expires_at).getTime(), 'expired at ' + data.download.expires_at + ': run request 0 for a fresh one').to.be.above(Date.now()));
console.log('The webhook announces ' + data.size_bytes + ' bytes, sha256 ' + data.sha256 + ', link valid until ' + data.download.expires_at);

item.name: 3  Download the file and verify it

request.description: The signed link, untouched. No credentials of any kind: the link is the permission.

exec: const bytes = pm.response.stream;   // the raw bytes of the file
// SHA-256 of the bytes: the Web Crypto API where the Postman version has it, CryptoJS on older versions
pm.test('size is what the webhook announced', () => pm.expect(bytes.length).to.eql(Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('announcedSize'))));

item.name: 4  Break it: one character of sig= changed (expect 403)

exec: pm.test('the storage service does not say which part was wrong', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.include('AuthorizationFailure'));
